questions.stem: Which of the following defines communication?
questions.key: The process by which information is exchanged between individuals through a common system of symbols, signs, or behavior
distractors: Anything that prevents you from receiving and understanding the messages
The facility being used for communicating
The steps we take to successfully communicate
questions.explanation: Slide 22 quotes Webster: communication is the process by which information is exchanged between individuals through a common system of symbols, signs or behavior.
why: That defines a communication barrier.
That defines communications, with an s.
That describes the communication process.

questions.stem: It is the facility being used for communicating.
questions.explanation: Slide 33 says communications is the facility being used for communicating, while communication is the process of transmitting information.
why: Communication is the process of transmitting information from one person or place to another.
The communication process is the steps taken to communicate successfully.
A barrier prevents receiving and understanding messages.

questions.stem: It is anything that prevents you from receiving and understanding the messages.
questions.explanation: Slide 48 defines a communication barrier as anything that prevents you from receiving and understanding messages.
why: Feedback is a response in the two-way process, not an obstacle.
The communication process is the steps to communicate successfully.
Communications is the facility used for communicating.

questions.stem: Which list contains the four methods to communicate?
questions.key: Spoken word, body language, written, visual
distractors: Spoken word, body language, written, downward
questions.explanation: The methods of communication are spoken word, body language, written and visual.
why: Downward is a type of communication, not a method.
Upward is a type of communication, not a method.
Lateral is a type of communication, not a method.

questions.stem: Which list contains the three types of communication?
distractors: Spoken word, upward, lateral or horizontal
questions.explanation: Slides 29 and 35 list the three types of communication as downward, upward and lateral or horizontal. Spoken, written and visual are methods, not types.
why: Written is a method of communication, not a type.
Spoken word is a method of communication, not a type.
Visual is a method of communication, not a type.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the linear model of the communication process?
questions.key: Who says what, through what channel, to whom, with what effect
distractors: Sender and receiver exchange a message with feedback, and each can play both roles
Information moves downward, upward, or laterally within the organization
Spoken word, body language, written, and visual messages
questions.explanation: Slide 38 shows the linear model as: who says what, through what channel, to whom, with what effect.
why: That describes the two-way model.
That describes the types of communication.
Those are the methods to communicate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a barrier to communication?
questions.explanation: Active listening is a way to overcome barriers. Jargon, differences in perception and cultural differences are listed as barriers.
why: Jargon is listed as a barrier.
Differences in perception are listed as a barrier.
Cultural differences are listed as a barrier.

questions.stem: A soldier with a hearing difficulty misses part of a briefing. Which category of barrier is this?
questions.explanation: Physical disabilities in hearing or speech are physiological barriers, one of the five categories.
why: Language barriers involve jargon or language differences.
Psychological barriers involve emotion and the mental state of the receiver.
Attitudinal barriers involve attitudes toward the message or sender.

questions.stem: A briefing is full of unexplained technical terms and acronyms, and new soldiers miss the point. Which category of barrier is at work?
questions.explanation: The use of jargon and language differences fall under language barriers.
why: Psychological barriers involve emotion.
Physical barriers involve the environment or distance, not word choice.
Attitudinal barriers involve attitudes, not unclear wording.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the core communication technique of Active Listening?
questions.key: Listening to understand rather than just to reply
distractors: Keeping messages brief, direct, and free of unnecessary jargon
Being mindful of tone and nonverbal cues and keeping open body language
Focusing objectively on the situation rather than attacking the person
questions.explanation: Active listening means listening to understand rather than just to reply, focusing on the speaker and not preparing your next argument.
why: That describes clarity and conciseness.
That describes emotional intelligence.
That describes constructive feedback.

questions.stem: This communication tool is used for face-to-face discussions and building rapport remotely.
questions.explanation: Slide 20 lists video conferencing for face-to-face discussions and rapport building at a distance.
why: Instant messaging is for quick, real-time collaboration and updates.
Project tracking and alignment helps members understand goals and timelines.
Written memos are a written method, not one of the essential tools listed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a way to overcome communication barriers?
questions.explanation: Slides 51-55 list listening actively, using simple language and giving constructive feedback as ways to overcome barriers. Slide 54 advises not interrupting the other person.
why: This is a listed way to overcome barriers.
This is a listed way to overcome barriers.
This is a listed way to overcome barriers.
